instructions: Finely chop 1/2 cup of the onion and 1/2 cup of the tomato. Chop 4 tbsp of the cilantro and grate 1 tsp of the ginger.
In a large bowl, whisk the gram flour, carom seeds, turmeric, chili powder, asafoetida and salt together.

Stir in the onion, tomato, cilantro and ginger. Add 3/4 cup water and beat with a fork for 1 to 2 minutes, until you have a thick batter that coats a spoon. If it runs, whisk in another spoonful of gram flour.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over low to medium heat and add 1 tbsp of the oil.
Spread a generous layer of batter over one side of 4 slices of bread and place them batter-side down in the pan.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the batter sets and the bread lifts easily from the pan.
Spread batter over the top of each slice and flip. Cook for 3 minutes, until the batter is set and golden. Transfer to a plate.
Wipe the pan, add another 1 tbsp oil, and repeat with the other 4 slices and the rest of the batter. Add the last 1 tbsp oil if the pan looks dry.
method_notes: Swasthi's (the lead, 4.97 from 51) coats the bread in a thick besan and vegetable batter and pan-fries it on both sides. Hebbar's Kitchen (5 from 32) does almost the same with a thinner batter and more vegetables. Written for 4 by multiplying the lead's 2-slice amounts by four. Ghee is swapped for oil, and the lead's optional green chili is left out to keep it mild.
